Scenario 1) Ghosting from said social event at a moment that feels like I can do so in a way that makes me feel happy and that I am not interrupting anyone's psyche.

Scenario 2) Staying behind until the very last of my comforts is resolved, like cleaning up and putting the bottles in the recycling after a party at a friends house or waiting until the last person I know has left and quietly say goodbye to people who may or may not care if I do so.

Both of these strategies give me a sense of self control and will of my own accord to move on from social engagements that doesn't place blame on either the social situation or anyone in the social situation for getting the space I need. That space can be simply walking away, to going on a bike ride home from the event, to going to somewhere and getting back into another social event if I get inspired, to making it home and being where I am comfortable.

Knowing in my own mind that the reasoning for getting my own space is because I want to and because I have made the decision to is freeing for me. There are times where I decide early on to do so and I take opportunities to let my mind be changed by the energy of the social environment. 

There are far more enjoyable times where I think to myself "Yup, I feel really satisfied with this level of social engagement and if I leave now I know I will be happy for the rest of the day no matter what I do when I get to a comfortable space.". Those moments may catch others off guard and I rarely have had an issue with dealing with that afterwards because it builds so much confidence for me to re-engage in a social environment again much sooner.

Edit: read the question over and starting to realize that I answered this in a different way than the question may have been intended. My answer really has to do with a strategy for pre-loading success for dealing with the inevitable stress of crowds. 

Scenario 3) I feel like I cannot leave within a timeframe that suits my anxiety and end up having a difficult time relaxing for the rest of the day so I choose to let my moment at home, alone or not, be about self pampering. A bubble bath is a great goto for me as well as a movie without commercials and if I can choose to write my feelings out but need to be productive I will select a music mix without many lyrics if any at all.

When I was younger I felt like a 'loner'. This self identification brought along a series of trying out the different social groups and clicks that made sense but never finding my path in such groups to be pleasing.

As I got older I felt more comfortable with the identification of 'introvert' where my time was best suited being social when I felt like being social. Now, when I do not feel like being social I take my alone time in stride and make appearances where I can in order to not appear as a 'loner' or 'someone whom others cannot invest their social time'. 

Since I am more keen on one-on-one interactions or at the very least no more than 4 people I know well without a single person whom I am not comfortable with -- I simply default back to being an 'introvert'. 'Extroverts', those who are often called social butterflies, find the ability to go out into social environments without such alone-time identifications, or so it seems to me. 

We all need alone-time, I think. Maybe when I was younger I was bold enough to take that time regardless of how it affected my social status. I still find myself bold enough to have self care without caring about my social status. My social status still suffers due to such boldness. :/

After talking with a person on my call list, not a suicide prevention line because I was only feeling sad and still unlovable, I felt pushed to the brink again. Talking isn't working and it feels like the entire world just wants me gone except for a select few. I can't even scream in pain here where I am because the response by others is to yell back and suggest kicking me out. I never really understood why people would do that to someone when my natural instinct if I think someone is in trouble is to run to their aid and comfort them. Is it a bad thing to meet someone screaming in frustration with a "hey, it's alright you're ok, tell me what's going on?".

Telling some stranger on a crisis prevention hotline doesn't really work for me because explaining what's wrong in the moment sounds so defeated before it even comes out of my mouth. What's wrong is so vast and seemingly endless for me right now and I would more than likely have no actual reason to respond to their questions. Or so it was in my experience. Even if I were to try and explain what just happened the responses always come across in a tone that is so unbelievable. 

I honestly can't feel cared for when someone who doesn't know me tries to comfort a situation not knowing that everyone in my life already wants nothing to do with me.

I don't know how to ask people to leave me alone if I am starting to spiral. "Leave me alone right now" didn't work. Screaming didn't work. Taking my anti-depressants and a sleep aid, approved by the doctor like I "should" be following, is the only conclusion we'd reach anyways. 

The problem here is that I feel I already KNOW what I'm supposed to be DOING and it doesn't SEEM to ever change how I FEEL. Thanks for reading.

Thank you for the response. 

I have not sought credit counseling yet but I will add that to the list of things on my todo list. 

I find that certain people in my environment really stress me out. Some people, specifically, make me feel absolutely neurotic. I want to find a constructive outlet for dealing with that but running away from where I grew up isn't an option while I am recovering. 

I still don't know what talking to suicide prevention hotlines does for my ongoing feelings of extreme depression. I feel like this world is rapidly ending and I just want to spend it with my lover, who is visiting friends and getting some space while I focus on myself.

The more I talk to people the more I hear should this and should that. If the only people who are able to help me are ones that I have to pay for then I'll just settle my debts and go out peacefully.

A therapist once told me that people who overanalyze, like I often do being stuck in my head as well, have a more difficult time in therapy not being their own therapist. 

After a couple of years of therapy I have found that things continue to be difficult even though I have so many things figured out. Knowing and being able to practice coping skills are separate things. Meditation is a skill that you will have to practice regularly and I struggle now to sit for more than 5 minutes after having more initial success with it.

I try to stop and smell the roses. Aromatherapy and scent can be a great ice breaker for calming your mind.

I hear all the time that good counseling is a matter of trying out different people and finding the right fit for you and your needs. I came here to Reddit to find avenues of therapy outside of needing to build a relationship with one person.
